evidence_works.work: Dell 1981, La langue bai: phonologie et lexique (Paris: Éditions de l'EHESS; chap. 2 'Système phonique du bai de Da-li', sec. 2.4 'Le système tonal', pp. 29-34)
evidence_works.detail: Describes the 'bai de Da-li' of a single consultant from a locality near Dali (p. 21); the entry's Wang 2006 table describes Zhoucheng (ZC), whose consultant was born in Zhoucheng village (Wang 2006 p. States that every syllable carries a tone as necessary to its identity as the initial or the final, and that there is no position in the chain where all tonal distinctions are neutralised, unlike the Pekingese 'neutral tone' ('Chaque syllabe porte un ton, aussi nécessaire à son identification que l'initiale ou la finale. Il n'existe pas dans la chaîne de position où toutes les distinctions tonales sont neutralisées, comme dans le cas du "ton neutre" du pékinois.', p. 29). Distinguishes pre-pausal (PP) syllables (before a pause or major syntactic break, incl. monosyllables and final syllables of polysyllables in isolation) from non-pre-pausal (NPP) syllables: eight tones in PP syllables, seven in NPP where T3 and T4 merge ('Le système tonal présente un paradigme de huit unités en syllabe PP, et de sept seulement en syllabe NPP, où les tons 3 et 4 sont confondus.', p. 29). T7, long low and inflected (212/211) in isolation, is realised whenever preceded by another syllable as a low punctual tone 'qui donne une impression auditive semblable à celle du "ton neutre" pékinois lorsqu'il suit une syllabe au quatrième ton' (p. 32): an auditory resemblance to a neutral tone, explicitly not a neutralisation. Instrumental part: on 68 isolated monosyllables recorded by G.K.C., rhyme duration measured from release of the initial to the last glottal pulse varies by tone nearly threefold ('la durée de la finale varie presque du simple au triple selon le ton', p. 33), the three level tones lying midway. 8-43.
evidence_works.loc: p. 29, T7 remark p. 32, duration measurements p. 33, discussion continuing on p. 34

tn.quote: Il existe deux tons de base bas et haut. Cette tonologie présente un certain nombre de spécificités qui ne paraissent pas être claires: elle est déplacée par endroits aussi bien au milieu qu'au début de la phrase. ... Ce qui est clair est que les substantifs ont généralement un ton haut sur le PN. Ceux qui comportent un augment ont un ton haut sur celui-ci et le PN porte un ton descendant (bref ?) là où on s'attendrait à un bas. ... Existent deux tons de base (bas et haut), avec possibilités d'obtenir des tons doubles (descendant et montant).
tn.translation: There are two basic tones, low and high. This tonology shows a number of peculiarities that do not seem clear: it is displaced in places, both in the middle and at the beginning of the sentence. ... What is clear is that nouns generally have a high tone on the nominal prefix. Those that carry an augment have a high tone on it and the nominal prefix bears a (short?) falling tone where one would expect a low. ... There are two basic tones (low and high), with the possibility of obtaining double tones (falling and rising).

5376.idn: Name in the source: Le tupuri; Tüpürï, /jäãk tüpürï/ ‘langue toupouri’; noms alternatifs: tüpürï, toupouri, toubouri, tpuri; family in the source: famille Niger-Congo, embranchement Adamawa-Oubangui, branche Adamawa, groupe 6 Mbum, sous-groupe Northern

tn.quote: Le tupuri est une langue à quatre hauteurs tonales. Les paires minimales sont imparfaites. Les consonnes obstruantes sonores et continues ont provoqué un abaissement tonal qui donne lieu à un ton infra-bas. ... Le ton mi-bas provient de l’abaissement d’un ton mi-haut d’un schème mi-haut mi-bas. Les voyelles fermées après consonne sourde tendent à élever le registre mi-haut jusqu’à un registre haut. ... La structure syllabique étant en syllabe ouverte, en contexte, le timbre d’une voyelle finale est élidé, le ton de cette syllabe étant amalgamé aux tons de la syllabe qui suit.
tn.translation: Tupuri is a language with four tone heights. Minimal pairs are imperfect. Voiced obstruents and continuants caused a tonal lowering that gives rise to an infra-low tone. ... The mid-low tone comes from the lowering of a mid-high tone of a mid-high mid-low scheme. Close vowels after a voiceless consonant tend to raise the mid-high register up to a high register. ... Syllable structure being open, in context the quality of a final vowel is elided, the tone of that syllable being merged with the tones of the following syllable.
tn.cite: Ruelland, Suzanne 2010. Le tupuri. Sorosoro (Pour que vivent les langues du monde), language page 'réalisée par Suzanne Ruelland' (LACITO/LLACAN), published 2010-07-15, updated 2010-08-19; section 'Précisions linguistiques' + 'Sources & bibliographie'. https://www.sorosoro.org/le-tupuri/
tn.locator: web page, section 'Précisions linguistiques'
tn.note: Four level tone heights (high, mid-high, mid-low, infra-low), extremes described as arising from consonant/vowel conditioning; labels gathered from prose, no table; no forms with tone labels shown. Checked against the source (tone consistency check, 2026-09-23): evidence impressionistic -> alternations (web page, section 'Précisions linguistiques').

corr.words: Ce phénomène s’observe dans les formes verbales injonctives, où les verbes ayant une consonne sourde à l’initiale ont un schème tonal mi-haut mi-haut, tandis que les verbes à l’injonctif ayant des consonnes sonores à l’initiale ont le schéma infra-bas mi-haut. Le ton mi-bas provient de l’abaissement d’un ton mi-haut d’un schème mi-haut mi-bas. ... La morpho-tonologie permet aussi d’élucider la création de quatre hauteurs tonales.

tn.quote: L'examen de la flexion vocalique de /a/ combinée avec celle des trois tons ne permet pas de donner aussi facilement des traductions dégagées de tout contexte. Dressons d'abord un tableau des variations formelles. [table: MOYEN HAUT BAS] Les six formes obtenues ne sont pas indépendantes les unes des autres. Elles ne présentent pas des oppositions individuelles de façon ponctuelle; mais /a/ et /e/ s'opposent pour chacun des trois tonèmes selon le champ (b); moyen s'oppose à bas et haut selon le champ (d), et haut à bas selon le champ (f).
tn.translation: Examining the vocalic inflection of /a/ combined with that of the three tones does not so easily allow translations free of all context. Let us first draw up a table of the formal variations. [table: MID HIGH LOW] The six forms obtained are not independent of one another. They do not present individual oppositions in a point-by-point way; rather /a/ and /e/ are opposed for each of the three tonemes according to field (b); mid is opposed to low and high according to field (d), and high to low according to field (f).

tn.quote: A group of eighty seven nouns were checked for tone and divided into groups having the same tonal melody. Almost all nouns so considered were disyllabic with a syllabic prefix and a monosyllabic stem. Six categories were formed by the grouping process, each of which is characterized by a sequence of two “level” tones drawn from the set (L, M, H). … there is good evidence that the language can be classified as a “three tone level” language, and probably not a two- or four- tone level language. The second is the clear dominance of the M–M group …

5384.idn: Name in the source: Bana; family in the source: Chadic: Centre-Est or A side of the Centre or Biu-Mandara branch of Central Chadic; most closely related to Higi and Kapsiki/Psikye, also Margi

tn.quote: That Bana has two contrasting tones, high and low, is easily demonstrated. All tone patterns are possible for all parts of speech, but monomorphemic uninflected verbs prefer simple tone patterns. Phonetic rising and falling tones, which are rare, are best analyzed under an autosegmental approach as two tones docking on a single syllable. … Bana, then, has two contrasting tones, high and low, which may occur in any tone pattern. The phonetic contour tones are in fact only combinations of simple tones.
tn.cite: Hofmann, Erica. 1990. A Preliminary Phonology of Bana. MA thesis, Department of Linguistics, University of Victoria. xii+275 pp. (SIL archive no. 9718)
tn.locator: Chapter VI 'Tone', opening paragraph, thesis p. 93 + 6.4 'A Two Tone System', thesis p. 101
tn.note: Two level tones, high and low, one per syllable in any combination (HH, HL, LH, LL, all three-syllable patterns); rare surface rises and falls are two tones on one syllable, some from floating tones.

tn.quote: 3.8 Fonem Suprasegmental Fonem suprasegmental tidak terdapat dalam bahasa Bosap. Tekanan [s] (stress), nada (pitch), panjang pendek (quantity), dan jeda (pause) tidak membedakaii arti suatu kata. Kata [nipa] 'ular' dengan tekanan path suku pertama dari belakang tidak berbeda artinya dengan tekanan path suku ke dua dari belakang /nipd/ Contoh: [bua] 'buah [kona] 'kena' [tepa] 'tumbuk'
tn.translation: 3.8 Suprasegmental phonemes. Suprasegmental phonemes do not occur in the Bosap language. Stress, pitch (tone), length (quantity) and pause do not distinguish the meaning of a word. The word [nipa] 'snake' with stress on the last syllable does not differ in meaning from the same word with stress on the second syllable from the end /nipa'/. Examples: [bua] 'fruit', [kona] 'hit, affected', [tepa] 'pound'.
tn.cite: Ibrahim, Sjahrial S. A. R., Rustam Effendi & M. P. Lambut. 1991. Struktur Bahasa Bosap. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa, Departemen Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan. xv+144 pp.

tn.note: No tone: the grammar states Bosap has no suprasegmental phonemes; pitch, stress, length and pause do not distinguish word meanings.

tn.quote: nous faisons l’hypothèse que ces consonnes nasales homorganiques sont des consonnes syllabiques. Notre hypothèse repose sur le fait que ces sons sont toujours porteurs de tons, en l’occurrence le ton bas [ ̀]. En portant le ton bas [ ̀], ces nasales assument une fonction de syllabes dans le mot. Elles se distinguent donc des consonnes dites ‘‘prénasalisées’’ qui elles, ne portent aucun ton. … Le trait différentiel est plutôt le trait [U0], vue que [H-] et [L-] sont des traits de tons (haut et bas).
tn.translation: we hypothesise that these homorganic nasal consonants are syllabic consonants. Our hypothesis rests on the fact that these sounds always bear tones, namely the low tone [ ̀]. By bearing the low tone [ ̀], these nasals take on the function of syllables in the word. They thus differ from the so-called 'prenasalised' consonants, which bear no tone. … The differentiating feature is rather [U0], given that [H-] and [L-] are tone features (high and low).
tn.cite: Kakou, Foba Antoine. 2021. La morphophonologie des consonnes nasales syllabiques du bétiné (éotilé), langue kwa de Côte d'Ivoire. Akofena n°004, Vol. 2: 205-218. Abidjan: Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny.
tn.locator: p. 208, section 1.2 'Analyse et interprétations' and p. 212, discussion of representation (12)
tn.note: High and low tones; a tone-bearing segment counts as a syllable, so the plural nasal prefix, always low-toned, is syllabic. Transcriptions also show unexplained macron (mid) marks. Checked against the source (tone consistency check, 2026-09-23): number of tones 2 -> not stated (p. 207 sec. 1.1 (01); p. 212 after (12); p. 214); contour tones no -> not stated (p. 212 (discussion of representation (12)); p. 213, section 2.1, corpus (14)).

tn.quote: 1.2.4 Tons et syllabes INVENTAIRE DES TONS Il existe, comme on s’en est deja apergu, deux tons de base, simples (bas et haut) et deux tons doubles (descendant et montant). Ces derniers trouvent presque tous leur origine dans la perte d’une consonne intervocalique en diachronie (41b). Avec les tons simples toutes les combinaisons dans les themes nominaux et adjectifs sont permises: HH, HB, BB, BH. … VALEUR DES TONS Les tons ont une valeur lexicale et grammaticale. … Contraction tonale. … Les différentes possibilités sont les suivantes: °H+H > H, °H+B > D, °B+B > B, °B+H > M.
tn.translation: 1.2.4 Tones and syllables. TONE INVENTORY. There are, as already noticed, two basic, simple tones (low and high) and two double tones (falling and rising). The latter almost all originate in the diachronic loss of an intervocalic consonant (41b). With the simple tones all combinations are permitted in nominal and adjectival stems: HH, HL, LL, LH. … VALUE OF THE TONES. The tones have lexical and grammatical value. … Tonal contraction. … The possibilities are: H+H > H, H+L > Falling, L+L > L, L+H > Rising.
tn.cite: Motingea Mangulu, André. 2008. Aspects du bongili de la Sangha-Likouala, suivis de l'esquisse du parler énga de Mampoko, Lulonga. (ILCAA Language Monograph Series.) Tokyo: ILCAA, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.
tn.locator: sec. 1.2.4 'Tons et syllabes', pp. 14-15
tn.note: Two basic level tones, low and high, with lexical and grammatical value; falling and rising 'double' tones arise from vowel contraction or old consonant loss; a low tonal morpheme marks some tenses. Checked against the source (tone consistency check round 3, 2026-09-24): evidence impressionistic -> alternations (sec. 1.2.4, REGLES TONALES, pp. 15-16).

corr.words: Les principales règles tonales sont les suivantes : la contraction, l'harmonie, le contraste, la neutralisation, l'abaissement et la propagation. ... L'abaissement tonal est constaté aux tiroirs de l'optatif, du passé proche et du futur négatif dans lesquels le morphotonème lexical haut du radical reste invariablement bas.

tn.quote: （三）声调及符号（11 个调） 第一类调为： （1）42 调，调号：b；例词：sainb 年，aob 二，gab 药。 （2）22 调，调号：p；例词：sainp 新，wewp 石灰，wap 树。 第二类调为： 55 调；调号：x；例词：sainx 钱 … 第三类调为： （1）53 调，调号：d … （2）232 调，调号：z … 第四类调为： 11 调；调号：l … 第五类调为： （1）55 调，调号：t … （2）24 调，调号：c … 第六类调为： （1）13 调，调号：s … （2）22 调，调号：p … 第七类调为： （1）33 调，调号：k … （2）13 调，调号：s … 第八类调为： 21 调；调号：f；例词：saif 下巴，duf 豆
tn.translation: (3) Tones and tone letters (11 tones). Category-1 tones: (1) value 42, letter b; examples sainb 'year', aob 'two', gab 'medicine'. (2) value 22, letter p; examples sainp 'new', wewp 'lime', wap 'tree'. Category 2: value 55, letter x; sainx 'money' ... Category 3: (1) 53, letter d ... (2) 232, letter z ... Category 4: 11, letter l ... Category 5: (1) 55, letter t ... (2) 24, letter c ... Category 6: (1) 13, letter s ... (2) 22, letter p ... Category 7: (1) 33, letter k ... (2) 13, letter s ... Category 8: 21, letter f; examples saif 'chin', duf 'bean'.
tn.cite: 吴正彪 (Wu Zhengbiao) & 杨光应 (Yang Guangying). 2010. 麻山次方言区苗文方案的设计与使用——兼谈苗族英雄史诗《亚鲁王》的记译整理问题. 民族翻译 (Minzu Fanyi) 2010(3) (cumulative no. 76): 58-65. Article no. 1674-280X(2010)03-0058-08.

tn.note: Eleven tones written with tone letters, spread over the eight historical Miao categories: levels 55, 33, 22, 11 and contours 42, 53, 232, 24, 13, 21; every syllable carries a tone letter. Checked against the source (tone consistency check round 3, 2026-09-24): domain every syllable -> unstated (p. 63).

corr.words: 诚然，在对麻山次方言苗文符号的设计过程中，由于调查的语音点有限，可能有个别音节尚未发现而没有把它的符号拟定出来，对这一问题也只有在这套苗文的使用过程中不断地深化后有新的发现时再继续补充完善。 ... 同样，在“母本”的苗文符号中只有八个用来表示声调符号的字母，而麻山次方言中普遍存在十一个调值的现象，我们只有在原有声调符号的基础上增加了三个声调符号 p、z、c，这也是符号记音的科学要求。

5394.idn: Name in the source: Chumburung; family in the source: a North Guang language; the Guang family belongs to the Tano subgroup of Kwa languages

tn.quote: Chumburung has two contrastive tone levels, high tone and low tone. Unless the word ends in a glottal stop, pre-pausal low tones are always realized as low falling pitches. … In addition there is a lexical process of high tone spreading in which high tones, regardless of where they occur in the word, spread rightward to the right edge of the word. … Finally, the language has both automatic and nonautomatic downstep of high tones, which is the focus of the present work. … Next, we look at nonautomatic downstep, which is downstep caused by a floating low tone.
tn.cite: Snider, Keith. 2007. Automatic and nonautomatic downstep in Chumburung: an instrumental comparison. Journal of West African Languages 34(1): 105-114.
tn.locator: pp.106-108, section 1 'Tone in Chumburung'
tn.note: Two contrastive level tones, high and low; lexical and postlexical high-tone spreading; automatic and nonautomatic downstep of high, the latter triggered by a floating low tone.

5395.idn: Name in the source: Chori; family in the source: Plantoid, Niger Congo

tn.quote: Finally, Dihoff (1976) reported a six-level system in Chori [Plantoid, Niger Congo; Nigeria]. But he notes that dictionary entries require only three underlying tones: Level 1 (highest), Level 4, and Level 6 (lowest). Therefore, it appears that the six levels are not contrastive.
tn.cite: Akinlabi, Akinbiyi, Firmin Ahoua & Bleu Gildas Gondo. 2022. On five-level tone contrasts: The case of Dan-Gblewo. Stellenbosch Papers in Linguistics Plus 62(2): 35-50. doi:10.5842/62-2-908.
tn.locator: p. 37, sec. 2 'Reported contrastive pitch levels'
tn.note: Six phonetic pitch levels reported (Dihoff 1976), but only three underlying level tones are contrastive: levels 1 (highest), 4 and 6 (lowest). Second-hand summary; no Chori forms shown.

5395.cfw: Known only second-hand: Akinlabi et al. 2022 reports the tone system after another work; the primary description was not read.

Voiced series (Low tone) … In the case of the tone of syllables which began with voiceless sounds, there is another type in Monpa (Mama) besides the type with the 53 tone.
